has raised US$25 million in Series A funding to build websites that generate, test and deploy changes continuously rather than wait for the next manual optimization cycle. The San Francisco company is applying AI agents to a part of marketing still dominated by experimentation queues, design reviews and engineering tickets.
Reported conversion and customer-revenue gains are company claims that marketers still need to validate independently.

The most striking numbers in the announcement concern customer results. Coframe says its platform has generated more than US$300 million in incremental customer revenue and achieved average conversion-rate improvement above 20%. It also describes large lifts for named clients, including Dropbox, Replit and Cash App.
More than US$300 million in incremental customer revenue and over 20% average conversion improvement.

For marketers, the missing details matter as much as the headline figures. A conversion lift from one landing page may be difficult to extrapolate across an entire website. Results can be influenced by traffic mix, seasonality, campaign spend, baseline performance and the duration of an experiment. Revenue attribution is especially sensitive to how the counterfactual is constructed.

But website optimization is not only a question of maximizing clicks. An AI system can unintentionally favor misleading urgency, inaccessible layouts or aggressive personalization if those tactics improve a narrow metric. Teams need constraints for brand consistency, user consent, accessibility and legal claims before allowing software to alter live customer experiences.

The new funding gives Coframe resources to pursue a more automated website stack. For marketers, the relevant test is narrower: can it shorten experiment cycles while preserving evidence quality and customer trust? Until the claimed gains are reproducible under clear measurement conditions, the strongest takeaway is a faster way to test, not a guaranteed faster way to grow.
